selection: Targeted follow-up of the DTNA averaging-set request left without a request-specific disposition inside section 2.5. Search terms were 1037.740 and averaging-set limitations/limits in the full official response-document text. Matches led to section 10.3.2. This is not a new comment sample or a census of section 10.3.2.
studyScope: Historical April 2023 proposal, March 2024 agency response and April 2024 published final text only. No claim about currently operative law or a complete subsequent amendment history.
sourceAuthentication: Visual review of specified official PDF pages and checks of their hashes against the existing pilot. Offline projections and fingerprints bind the saved coding to that review; they do not independently authenticate source bytes or manual interpretation.

response.reviewScope: DTNA's reproduced block, the complete section summary and response, with neighboring text visible on the same pages. Other organizations' original blocks in this eleven-page section were not all read or inventoried. Section 11 follows the response and is not coded.

proposed.reviewScope: Preamble section III.A.3, Other Potential HD CO2 Emission Credit Flexibilities. The invitation to comment on a potential interim option is not an adopted baseline provision.

final.reviewScope: Published 40 CFR 1037.150(z), 1037.720(a), and amendatory instruction 108 for 1037.740, with adjacent credit-correction clauses distinguished from transfer rules. Not an exhaustive review of all cross-referenced credit provisions or of parts 86/1036.

reviews.matchRationale: Both reproduced blocks cite DTNA's EPA-HQ-OAR-2022-0985-1555-A1 and ask to exempt ZEV ABT credits from 1037.740 averaging-set limits. The section 2.5 excerpt cites pages 167-168; section 10.3.2 reproduces the detailed request on pages 74-75 and a repeated answer on page 171. These are agency-selected representations of one matched request, not independently read originals or new observations.
reviews.responseSummary: The summary names DTNA and its requests for all-category ZEV transfers, no discount and program-life availability. The collective response retains weight-based averaging sets but adopts an interim vehicle-to-vehicle transfer flexibility for model years 2027-2032 without a volume cap. It does not finalize vehicle-credit transfers into engine averaging sets. These are shared decisions, not a separately named disposition addressed only to DTNA.
reviews.proposalContext: The April 2023 preamble already invited comment on a potential interim cross-set transfer provision beginning in MY2027 and ending after MY2032, with possible caps and other restrictions. The option predates the submission; final use of a related mechanism is not evidence DTNA originated or caused it.

facets.requested: Allow all ZEV credits to move among available vehicle categories.
facets.observed: The response describes interim cross-set vehicle-credit transfers. Published 1037.150(z)(1) allows credits generated under part 1037 to be used through MY2032 for the averaging sets in 1037.740(a); the latter retains Light, Medium and Heavy HDV sets.

facets.requested: Apply the flexibility throughout the Phase 3 program's life.
facets.observed: The collective response calls the allowance interim during MY2027-2032. The published clause permits use through MY2032, not a permanent exemption. It also covers specified pre-2027 advanced-technology credits, so generation eligibility must not be reduced to 2027-2032 alone.

facets.requested: Apply the flexibility to credits traded between manufacturers.
facets.observed: Published 1037.150(z)(3)-(4) permits trading redesignated credits subject to ordinary trading and other retained credit provisions; 1037.720(a) defines trading between manufacturers.

facets.requested: Allow the transfer without discounting credits.
facets.observed: The reviewed response says no volume cap for the interim vehicle transfers, which is not the same as a no-discount finding. The inspected transfer clause specifies no new transfer discount but retains other credit provisions; not all cross-references were audited. Adjacent 10-percent discounts concern correcting erroneous credit balances, not a general transfer discount.

reviews.remainingRequirements: Independently review the cross-section identity match, shared response and facet coding; obtain the version-matched original submission. A full cross-program implementation or no-discount claim additionally requires the other referenced provisions and any relevant later corrections. This targeted follow-up does not resolve the other two section-2.5 disposition gaps, establish a docket denominator or identify individual causal influence.
